title: Pullback maps between computing cup resolutions
statement: For a scheme morphism f:X′→X and modules F,G on X, there exist computing pairings D for F,G and E for f*F,f*G [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data], and additive global-section degree maps l,r,t on their left, right and target complexes. Each degree map commutes with the adjacent differential. In all degrees the left and right maps on cocycles induce the ordinary pullback maps [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], while the target map induces ordinary pullback on F tensor G followed by cohomology of the canonical tensor-pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. In every bidegree t(p+q)(D.pair(p,q,top)(a,b))=E.pair(p,q,top)(l(p)(a),r(q)(b)). Class equations hold for every source and target cycle with the stated equality of underlying sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. No cohomological cup product is specified and no equality of global-section rings is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the six computing resolutions by the functorial Godement stalk-product construction on X and X′. On each open of X the map to f_* of the first Godement term on X′ evaluates at f(x′) and applies the stalk map of the adjunction unit. Iterate this natural map through stalk products. Naturality with unit insertion and stalk evaluation makes it commute with cofaces and codegeneracies, hence with the alternating differential. Restrict to natural degrees and take global sections.

Use the stalkwise tensor pairing, followed by the Alexander--Whitney front and back faces. Coefficient maps commute with stalk tensors; for a scheme morphism use the section-normalized tensor-pullback comparison. The face maps are natural, so applying the resulting target map to each pairing is the pairing of the two mapped sections, with the same degrees and signs. This proves the section pairing equation.

Equip the six flasque complexes with computing injective comparisons as in exists_moduleCupResolutionPairing. For a class equation, push the target complex and its injective comparison forward to X. Both have flasque terms, since injectives are flasque and pushforward preserves flasque sheaves; no assertion that pushforward preserves injectives is made. Take a bounded-below injective replacement of the pushed-forward target injective complex on X. The replacement and pushed-forward comparison induce isomorphisms on global homology by acyclic-complex comparison. The two maps from the source resolution into this injective replacement extend the same adjunction unit and are homotopic by resolution comparison. Applying global homology and cancelling the computing isomorphisms identifies the map with the resolution ladder defining moduleCohomologyPullback. The target unit is followed by the tensor coefficient comparison; coefficient naturality gives the displayed target equation.

lean.statement:
theorem moduleCup_pullback_resolution_maps (X X' : Scheme.{v}) (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (F G : X.Modules) :
    ∃ (D : CupResolutionPairing F G)
      (E : CupResolutionPairing ((tensorPullback f).obj F) ((tensorPullback f).obj G))
      (l : ∀ n : ℕ, Γ(D.left.K.X n, ⊤) →+ Γ(E.left.K.X n, ⊤))
      (r : ∀ n : ℕ, Γ(D.right.K.X n, ⊤) →+ Γ(E.right.K.X n, ⊤))
      (t : ∀ n : ℕ, Γ(D.target.K.X n, ⊤) →+ Γ(E.target.K.X n, ⊤)),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Γ(D.left.K.X n, ⊤)),
        (E.left.K.d n (n + 1)).val.app (op ⊤) (l n a) =
          l (n + 1) ((D.left.K.d n (n + 1)).val.app (op ⊤) a)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Γ(D.right.K.X n, ⊤)),
        (E.right.K.d n (n + 1)).val.app (op ⊤) (r n a) =
          r (n + 1) ((D.right.K.d n (n + 1)).val.app (op ⊤) a)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Γ(D.target.K.X n, ⊤)),
        (E.target.K.d n (n + 1)).val.app (op ⊤) (t n a) =
          t (n + 1) ((D.target.K.d n (n + 1)).val.app (op ⊤) a)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ)
        (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (a' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.left.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        a'.val = l n a.val →
          E.left.class n a' =
            moduleCohomologyPullback f F n (D.left.class n a)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ)
        (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (a' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.right.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        a'.val = r n a.val →
          E.right.class n a' =
            moduleCohomologyPullback f G n (D.right.class n a)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ)
        (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (a' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X'.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.target.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        a'.val = t n a.val →
          E.target.class n a' =
            (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X'.toRingedSpace n).map
              ((Classical.choose (module_pullback_tensor f)) F G).hom
              (moduleCohomologyPullback f (@id X.Modules (F ⊗ G)) n
                (D.target.class n a))) ∧
      (∀ (p q : ℕ) (a : Γ(D.left.K.X p, ⊤)) (b : Γ(D.right.K.X q, ⊤)),
        t (p + q) (D.pair p q ⊤ a b) = E.pair p q ⊤ (l p a) (r q b))
